"RIVAL CIRCUIT — COMPLETE MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT
1. GAME OVERVIEW

Create an original, high-quality 2D side-view arcade fighting game called Rival Circuit.

The game must have a colorful, detailed, high-resolution pixel-art presentation inspired by the visual quality and atmosphere of classic arcade fighting games, while maintaining completely original characters, artwork, animations, stages, branding, music, and sound effects.

Main requirements
Mobile-first game designed for touchscreen devices.
Landscape orientation.
Single-player fighting against CPU-controlled opponents.
20 playable fighters: 10 male and 10 female.
7 unique fighting arenas.
Arcade Mode and Championship Mode.
Character-specific attacks, combos, and special moves.
Unlockable outfits, accessories, and finishing moves.
Earnable in-game currency.
Persistent save system.
Adjustable difficulty and control settings.
Original retro arcade music and sound effects.
Target 60 FPS where supported.

The game should be designed as a complete, enjoyable experience rather than a simple prototype.

No advertisements, subscriptions, loot boxes, or real-money purchases. All unlockable content must be obtainable through gameplay.

The intended selling price is $0.99, with the final App Store price configured separately.

2. VISUAL ART DIRECTION

This is one of the most important requirements.

Create a beautiful, highly detailed, colorful 2D pixel-art arcade fighting game.

The artwork should have the visual richness of later-generation classic arcade pixel art, sometimes described as 64-bit-style artwork. This refers to artistic detail and presentation, not computer architecture.

Fighter artwork

Every character must have:

A distinct, recognizable face.
Detailed facial expressions.
Natural human anatomy and proportions.
Individually designed hairstyles.
Detailed clothing, costumes, folds, and textures.
Carefully shaded skin, hair, and clothing.
Highlights, shadows, and strong color contrast.
A unique silhouette and fighting stance.
Expressive idle, attack, damage, and victory poses.
Environments

Backgrounds must be beautifully illustrated and detailed, with:

Architecture and environmental scenery.
Depth and multiple background layers.
Atmospheric lighting and shadows.
Detailed buildings, objects, and decorations.
Reflections and environmental effects where appropriate.
Animated scenery that makes each arena feel alive.
Pixel-art quality
Crisp, intentional pixel clusters.
Detailed pixel shading.
Rich color palettes.
Clean outlines.
Carefully animated sprites.
No blurry or smeared pixel art.
No unnecessary smoothing that destroys pixel detail.
Avoid
Minecraft-style or voxel characters.
Cube-shaped bodies.
Stick figures.
Basic geometric characters.
Generic 3D models.
Simplistic placeholder sprites.
Flat, empty backgrounds.
Static character images pretending to be animations.
Originality requirement

Everything must be independently designed.

Do not copy, trace, recreate, or closely imitate any existing game's characters, stages, sprites, animations, logos, HUD, music, sound effects, or other recognizable assets.

Create original characters, original fighting styles, original stages, original special moves, and original branding.

3. PLAYABLE CHARACTER ROSTER

Create 20 playable fighters with different appearances, personalities, fighting styles, strengths, weaknesses, and signature special moves.

Every fighter must have unique artwork and animations. Do not simply recolor an existing character.

Male fighters

1. Kenji

Fighting style: Karate.
Special move: Dragon Strike.
Appearance: Black hair, red headband, white martial arts uniform.
Balanced beginner-friendly fighter.

2. Bruno

Fighting style: Boxing.
Special move: Heavy Impact.
Appearance: Muscular build, blue boxing shorts and gloves.
High damage, slower movement.

3. Jae

Fighting style: Taekwondo.
Special move: Lightning Kick.
Appearance: Korean fighter wearing blue and white.
Fast, powerful kicking combinations.

4. Marcus

Fighting style: Street Fighting.
Special move: Ground Breaker.
Appearance: Black male fighter wearing a red sleeveless jacket.
Powerful attacks and aggressive combat.

5. Ryuji

Fighting style: Kenjutsu-inspired martial arts.
Special move: Blade Dance.
Appearance: Japanese fighter wearing dark blue, samurai-inspired clothing.
Weaponless precision fighting.

6. Axel

Fighting style: Kickboxing.
Special move: Rapid Assault.
Appearance: Blonde hair, black and gold outfit.
High speed and fast combinations.

7. Titan

Fighting style: Professional Wrestling.
Special move: Titan Slam.
Appearance: Large, muscular wrestler wearing a green wrestling outfit.
Powerful grappling attacks.

8. Liang

Fighting style: Kung Fu.
Special move: Dragon Combination.
Appearance: Chinese fighter wearing a detailed red traditional outfit.
Technical combinations and balanced attacks.

9. Dante

Fighting style: Capoeira.
Special move: Spinning Tempest.
Appearance: Fighter wearing yellow and green pants.
Evasive movement and spinning attacks.

10. Vex

Fighting style: Dark Martial Arts.
Special move: Shadow Burst.
Appearance: Tall fighter with silver hair and dark purple clothing.
Powerful special attacks.
Female fighters

All female fighters must be adults, athletic, stylish, and individually designed.

They must have distinct faces, hairstyles, body proportions, costumes, fighting stances, and animations. Avoid making them look like recolored versions of one another.

11. Maya

Fighting style: Kickboxing.
Special move: Cyclone Kick.
Appearance: Athletic build, long dark hair, purple outfit.
Fast and agile.

12. Akari

Fighting style: Ninjutsu.
Special move: Shadow Rush.
Appearance: Japanese fighter with dark ponytail and dark green ninja-inspired outfit.
Fast evasive movement.

13. Scarlett

Fighting style: Boxing.
Special move: Crimson Knockout.
Appearance: Blonde hair, red and white outfit.
High-power punches.

14. Nia

Fighting style: Taekwondo.
Special move: Skybreaker.
Appearance: Black fighter with braided hair and blue and white outfit.
Powerful kicking combinations.

15. Mei

Fighting style: Kung Fu.
Special move: Golden Dragon.
Appearance: Chinese fighter with long black hair and red and gold outfit.
Technical combinations.

16. Isabella

Fighting style: Capoeira.
Special move: Tropical Storm.
Appearance: Brazilian fighter with curly brown hair and green and yellow outfit.
High mobility and evasive attacks.

17. Raven

Fighting style: Wrestling.
Special move: Raven's Wrath.
Appearance: Red-haired wrestler wearing black and gold.
Powerful grappling attacks.

18. Yuna

Fighting style: Kenjutsu-inspired martial arts.
Special move: Moonlight Strike.
Appearance: Japanese fighter with black hair and white and red outfit.
Precise weaponless combat.

19. Vanessa

Fighting style: Street Fighting.
Special move: Street Fury.
Appearance: Short silver hair and black and red jacket.
Aggressive fighting style.

20. Seraphina

Fighting style: Mystic Martial Arts.
Special move: Celestial Burst.
Appearance: Long silver hair and purple and gold outfit.
Unique energy-based special attacks.
Character requirements

Each fighter needs:

Health, attack, defense, speed, jump, and special-power statistics.
Unique idle animation.
Unique walking and jumping animations.
Unique attack animations.
Unique special move.
Unique victory and defeat animations.
At least two unlockable outfits.
Character-specific visual effects.

All 20 characters must be playable.

If the full roster cannot be completed in one generation, develop the game in stages without removing or changing the planned roster.

4. FIGHTING SYSTEM

Create a responsive one-on-one fighting system.

Match rules
Best of three rounds.
First fighter to win two rounds wins the match.
Each round lasts 60 seconds.
Display health bars for both fighters.
Display the current round.
Display a special-move meter.
KO occurs when a fighter's health reaches zero.
If time expires, the fighter with more health wins.
Implement a fair tie rule if health is exactly equal.
Touchscreen controls

The game must be fully playable using touchscreen controls.

Left side:

Virtual joystick for movement.
Left and right movement.
Up to jump.
Down to crouch.

Right side:

X = Punch.
A = Kick.
B = Block.
Y = Special attack when the special meter is charged.

If a virtual joystick is not supported, use directional buttons.

Controls must:

Be large enough for mobile screens.
Have comfortable spacing.
Respond quickly.
Support simultaneous movement and attacking.
Avoid overlapping the health bars or other HUD elements.
Adapt to phone and tablet landscape screens.
Allow adjustable size and transparency.

Do not require a physical controller or keyboard.

Combat mechanics

Implement:

Light and heavy punches.
Light and heavy kicks.
High and low attacks.
Jump attacks.
Crouching attacks.
Combos.
Blocking.
Counters.
Dodging and evasion.
Special attacks.
Damage and knockback.
Stun and recovery.
Knockdowns and get-up animations.
Attack cooldowns.
Special-meter charging.

The special meter should increase when fighters successfully deal or receive damage.

Collision system — critical

Fighters must never pass through one another or overlap their bodies.

Separate physical collision boundaries from attack hitboxes.

Maintain proper spacing during:

Walking.
Running.
Jumping.
Attacking.
Blocking.
Knockback.
Special moves.

Prevent sliding, teleporting, drifting, and fighters moving outside the arena.

Attacks should connect through properly configured hitboxes, not through body overlap.

5. CPU OPPONENT AI

The opponent must actively fight the player.

Do not create an opponent that simply stands still or waits to be attacked.

The CPU must:

Approach the player.
Maintain appropriate fighting distance.
Punch and kick.
Perform combinations.
Jump and attack.
Crouch.
Block.
Evade.
Counter.
Use special attacks.
Pursue the player when necessary.
Recover after being hit.
React to the player's actions.

The CPU must follow the same combat rules, hitboxes, damage calculations, and cooldowns as the player.

Difficulty settings

Easy

Slower reactions.
Fewer combinations.
Less frequent blocking.
More mistakes.

Normal

Uses combinations.
Blocks and counters.
Uses special moves.
Provides a balanced challenge.

Hard

Faster reactions.
More strategic defense.
Punishes predictable attacks.
Uses combinations and special attacks effectively.
Fighting-style behavior

Make CPU behavior reflect each fighter's fighting style.

Examples:

Boxers prioritize punches.
Kickboxers combine punches and kicks.
Taekwondo fighters prioritize kicking combinations.
Wrestlers pursue grappling attacks.
Capoeira fighters use evasive spinning attacks.
Kung Fu fighters use technical combinations.
6. CHARACTER ANIMATIONS

Use actual animated pixel-art sprite frames.

Do not use a single static character image that simply moves around the screen.

Movement animations

Every fighter needs:

Idle breathing and fighting stance.
Walking forward.
Walking backward.
Running or dashing.
Jump preparation.
Jump rising.
Jump apex.
Falling.
Landing.
Forward and backward jumping.
Crouching.
Crouch transition.
Standing back up.
Attack animations

Include:

Fast punches.
Heavy punches.
Straight punches.
Hooks.
Uppercuts.
Body punches.
Light kicks.
Heavy kicks.
High kicks.
Low kicks.
Side kicks.
Roundhouse kicks.
Jump attacks.
Crouching attacks.
Combos.
Special-move preparation.
Special-move execution.
Special-move recovery.
Defensive and damage animations

Include:

Standing block.
Crouching block.
Block impact.
Dodging.
Evading.
Light hit reaction.
Heavy hit reaction.
Staggering.
Knockback.
Falling.
Ground impact.
Knockdown.
Getting back up.
Other animations
Unique victory pose.
Unique defeat animation.
Dramatic finishing animation.
Character-specific special-move animation.

Each attack must have:

Anticipation.
Execution.
Contact.
Recovery.

Suggested animation frame targets:

Idle: 8–12 frames.
Walking: 8 frames.
Running and jumping: 8–12 frames.
Punches: 6–10 frames per attack.
Kicks: 8–12 frames.
Combos: 12–20+ frames.
Special moves: 12–24+ frames.
Knockdown and recovery: 10–16 frames.

Animate limbs, torso, head, hair, and clothing naturally.

Avoid duplicated frames, frozen poses, snapping, and sliding animations.

7. VISUAL COMBAT EFFECTS

Add detailed pixel-art effects that make combat satisfying.

Include:

Impact flashes.
Sparks.
Brief hit-stop on powerful attacks.
Subtle screen shake on heavy attacks.
Dust from movement and landing.
Motion trails from fast punches and kicks.
Larger impact bursts from heavy attacks.
Stronger knockback from powerful moves.
Unique special-move energy effects.
Shockwaves and finishing effects.
Sparks when attacks are blocked.
Visual evasion effects.
Distinct critical-hit effects.
Dramatic KO presentation.

Each fighter should have visually distinctive special effects.

Effects must not obscure the fighters, interfere with hitboxes, or interfere with touchscreen controls.

Optimize effects for mobile performance.

8. AUDIO AND RETRO ARCADE MUSIC

Create original arcade-style sound effects and music.

Fighting sound effects

Include:

Light punches.
Heavy punches.
Kicks.
Uppercuts.
Blocking.
Footsteps.
Jumping and landing.
Dashing.
Hit reactions.
Heavy impacts.
Knockback and falling.
Special-move charging.
Unique special-move sounds for all 20 fighters.
KO sounds.
Victory and defeat sounds.
Crowd reactions.

Sound effects must synchronize with the actual animation and contact frames.

Heavy attacks should sound stronger than light attacks.

Avoid excessive repetition and overlapping audio.

Original retro music

Create original instrumental arcade music using retro-inspired sounds such as:

8-bit and 16-bit-inspired electronic instruments.
Retro synthesizers.
Electronic basslines.
Chiptune melodies.
Energetic percussion.
Catchy instrumental themes.
Dramatic arcade-style musical transitions.

Create separate original tracks for:

Main menu.
Character selection.
Each of the seven arenas.
Fighting matches.
Championship matches.
Final boss.
Victory.
Defeat.

Every track must be an original composition or properly licensed for commercial use.

Do not copy, sample, recreate, or closely imitate existing copyrighted songs, melodies, or game soundtracks.

Music and sound settings

Add separate controls in the Settings menu.

Background Music

ON/OFF toggle.
Adjustable volume slider.

Sound Effects

ON/OFF toggle.
Separate adjustable volume slider.

When background music is turned off, all background music must stop while sound effects can continue if enabled.

When music is turned back on, restore the previously selected volume.

Save audio preferences after closing and reopening the game.

Avoid repetitive tracks, abrupt transitions, excessive volume, and poor audio quality.

Optimize all audio for mobile devices.

9. FIGHTING ARENAS

Create seven distinct and detailed arenas.

Each arena must have its own atmosphere, background art, lighting, scenery, and environmental animations.

1. Neon City

Nighttime city street.
Colorful neon signs.
Detailed buildings and streetlights.
Flickering signs and windows.
Unlocked initially.

2. Dragon Dojo

Traditional Japanese training hall.
Detailed wooden floor.
Lanterns and traditional decorations.
Unlock after 3 wins.

3. Sunset Beach

Tropical beach.
Ocean and palm trees.
Beautiful sunset.
Moving waves and leaves.
Unlock after 6 wins.

4. Underground

Dark industrial warehouse.
Concrete and metal structures.
Flickering lights.
Steam and atmospheric effects.
Unlock after 10 wins.

5. Sky High

Rooftop fighting arena.
Large nighttime skyline.
Moving clouds.
Detailed city lights.
Unlock after 15 wins.

6. Forgotten Temple

Ancient temple.
Mountain scenery.
Detailed stone structures.
Moving leaves and environmental effects.
Unlock after Championship completion.

7. The Colosseum

Ancient Roman gladiator arena.
Detailed stone architecture.
Large spectator stands.
Animated crowd.
Banners and sunset lighting.
Unlock after defeating the final boss.

All unlocked arenas must remain available for replay.

10. LIVING ENVIRONMENTS

Make the arenas feel alive.

Add environmental animations such as:

Birds flying across the sky.
Birds landing on rooftops and taking off.
Moving clouds.
Swaying trees and palm trees.
Moving plants.
Flickering streetlights.
Flickering neon signs.
Building windows changing brightness.
Ocean waves.
Moving flags and banners.
Spectators cheering, clapping, and moving.
Floating dust.
Steam.
Falling leaves.

Environmental animations must remain behind the fighters and must never interfere with gameplay.

Each arena should have its own appropriate environmental details.

11. DAY AND NIGHT CYCLE

Implement an optional day-and-night cycle.

One complete cycle should take approximately 30 real-time minutes.

Gradually transition through:

Morning.
Afternoon.
Sunset.
Evening.
Night.

Include:

Changing sky colors.
Sun movement.
Moon and stars.
Moving clouds.
Changing lighting.
Changing shadows.
City lights becoming visible at night.
Beach sunsets with changing colors.

Fighters must always remain clearly visible.

Add settings for:

Automatic cycle.
Fixed daytime.
Fixed nighttime.

Indoor arenas can reflect changes through windows and ambient lighting.

The day-and-night cycle must not affect combat, damage, visibility of attacks, or performance.

12. GAME MODES
Arcade Mode
Select a fighter.
Fight a sequence of CPU opponents.
Progress through increasingly difficult matches.
Defeat the final opponent.
Earn Legend Coins.
Replay with different fighters.
Championship Mode
Progress through increasingly difficult opponents.
Win matches to advance.
Track championship progress.
Include a final championship challenge.
Award a completion bonus.
Final Boss

Use one of the existing roster fighters as the final boss, with an enhanced AI configuration.

The boss should:

Have a more challenging fighting style.
Use combinations and special attacks.
React intelligently.
Have a dramatic introduction.
Have a unique boss health display.
Have a dramatic defeat sequence.

Do not create an unfinished or stationary boss.

13. MAIN MENU AND CHARACTER SELECTION
Main menu

Include:

Play.
Championship.
Fighters.
Legends Market.
Arena Select.
Settings.

Create:

An original Rival Circuit logo.
Animated fighter artwork.
A polished arcade-style interface.
A visible Legend Coin balance.
Clear navigation.
Character selection

Display:

Character portrait.
Character name.
Fighting style.
Statistics.
Signature special move.
Unlock status.
Outfit selection.
Character preview.
Arena selection

Display:

Arena artwork.
Arena name.
Unlock requirement.
Locked or unlocked status.
14. LEGEND COINS AND PROGRESSION

Create an in-game currency called Legend Coins.

Coins must be earned through gameplay.

Rewards
Normal victory: 250 coins.
Victory without losing a round: 400 coins.
Perfect victory without taking damage: 600 coins.
Championship completion: 2,000 bonus coins.
Final boss defeat: 1,000 bonus coins.

Use the highest applicable match reward rather than paying overlapping match rewards multiple times.

Championship and final-boss bonuses are separate rewards.

Additional rules:

Losing must never remove coins.
Rewards must not duplicate when reopening a results screen.
Save the balance permanently.
Display rewards clearly after each match.
15. LEGENDS MARKET

Create an in-game cosmetics shop called Legends Market.

All items must be purchased using earned Legend Coins.

Suggested prices
Standard outfits: 1,000 coins.
Rare outfits: 2,500 coins.
Exclusive outfits: 7,500 coins.
Gloves: 500 coins.
Boots: 750 coins.
Hairstyles: 800 coins.
Headbands and masks: appropriately priced.
Finishing moves: 5,000 coins.
Shop requirements
Preview items before purchase.
Display prices and current coin balance.
Ask for purchase confirmation.
Allow equipping and unequipping.
Save purchased items.
Prevent duplicate purchases.
Never deduct coins if a purchase fails.
Display a clear insufficient-funds message.

No real-money purchases, loot boxes, advertisements, or subscriptions.

16. RESULTS SCREEN

After every match, display:

Winner and loser.
Round results.
Match performance.
Coins earned.
Current coin balance.

Provide:

Rematch.
Main Menu.
Continue Championship.

Prevent duplicate rewards if the player revisits or reopens the results screen.

17. SAVE SYSTEM

Save all important player progress.

Persist:

Coin balance.
Unlocked fighters.
Purchased outfits.
Equipped cosmetics.
Unlocked arenas.
Championship progress.
Championship completion.
Settings.
Music preferences.
Sound-effect preferences.
Control preferences.
Difficulty settings.

Progress must remain saved after closing and reopening the game.

Handle interruptions and unexpected app closures without unnecessarily losing progress.

18. SETTINGS

Include:

Background music ON/OFF.
Music volume.
Sound effects ON/OFF.
Sound-effects volume.
Difficulty selection.
Automatic day/night cycle.
Fixed daytime.
Fixed nighttime.
Touchscreen control size.
Touchscreen control transparency.
Other necessary mobile control settings.

Settings must be saved and restored correctly.

19. MOBILE PERFORMANCE AND FILE SIZE

Optimize the game for mobile phones and tablets.

Requirements:

Target 60 FPS where supported.
Responsive landscape interface.
Efficient sprite sheets.
Compressed audio.
Efficient animations.
Optimized environmental effects.
No unnecessary videos.
No unused assets.
Avoid unnecessarily large libraries.

Aim for approximately 50–80 MB if practical, and keep the exported game under 100 MB if possible.

Do not sacrifice character detail, background quality, or animation quality just to reach a file-size target.

Verify the actual exported file size instead of assuming it will meet the target.

20. DEVELOPMENT ORDER

Build the game in organized stages.

Do not attempt to create every feature at the expense of having a broken or unfinished foundation.

Stage 1 — Core playable prototype

Build:

Kenji.
Maya.
Neon City.
Player movement.
CPU movement and AI.
Punches and kicks.
Blocking.
Health bars.
Timer.
Hitboxes.
Proper physical collision.
Basic animations.
Touchscreen controls.

The first two fighters must be genuinely playable.

Stage 2 — Combat quality

Add:

More attacks.
Combos.
Special moves.
Damage reactions.
Knockdowns.
Get-up animations.
Victory and defeat animations.
Visual effects.
Sound effects.
Stage 3 — Full character roster

Add all 20 fighters.

Preserve the completed prototype and do not break existing characters.

Stage 4 — Arenas and environments

Add all seven arenas.

Add environmental animations and the day-and-night cycle.

Stage 5 — Game modes and progression

Add Arcade Mode, Championship Mode, the final boss, unlocks, and rewards.

Stage 6 — Market and save system

Add outfits, accessories, finishing moves, Legends Market, results screens, and persistent saving.

Stage 7 — Music and polish

Add original retro music, audio settings, final visual improvements, performance optimization, and complete testing.

21. MANDATORY TESTING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

Before considering the game finished, test every major system.

Combat testing

Verify:

Movement.
Jumping.
Crouching.
Punches.
Kicks.
Blocking.
Combos.
Special meter.
Special attacks.
Health calculations.
KO.
Rounds.
Timer.
Match winner.
Collision testing

Verify that fighters never:

Pass through each other.
Overlap bodies.
Slide through attacks.
Teleport.
Drift outside the arena.

Test collision during walking, jumping, attacks, knockback, and special moves.

AI testing

Verify that CPU opponents:

Approach the player.
Attack.
Block.
Use combos.
Use special moves.
React to damage.
Behave differently at each difficulty.
Animation testing

Verify:

No frozen animations.
No missing frames.
No unnatural snapping.
No sliding.
Attacks connect at the correct animation frames.
Every fighter has distinctive animations.
Audio testing

Verify:

Correct sound synchronization.
Heavy attacks sound stronger.
Blocking sounds different from normal hits.
Special moves have unique sounds.
Music volume works.
Music can be switched off independently.
Sound effects remain active when music is disabled.
Audio preferences persist after restarting.
Arena testing

Verify:

All seven arenas look distinct.
Environmental animations work.
Day-and-night transitions work.
Background effects do not interfere with combat.
Performance remains acceptable.
Progression testing

Verify:

Coins are awarded correctly.
Rewards never duplicate.
Shop purchases work.
Insufficient funds are handled correctly.
Cosmetics equip correctly.
Unlocks persist.
Saves survive closing and reopening the game.
Mobile testing

Verify:

Touchscreen controls respond correctly.
Buttons are easy to reach.
Controls do not overlap the HUD.
Landscape layout works on different screen sizes.
The game remains responsive during combat.
22. FINAL DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTIONS

Prioritize a genuinely playable and polished fighting game.

Do not:

Use placeholder artwork while claiming it is finished.
Use static images as a substitute for actual animations.
Create fake combat where the opponent does not fight.
Ignore collision problems.
Remove planned characters or arenas without explaining why.
Replace detailed pixel art with simplistic graphics.
Claim that a feature works unless it has actually been implemented.
Copy or trace artwork, characters, music, or other assets from existing games.

If all features cannot be completed in one generation, build a working foundation and continue in the development stages above.

Preserve completed work between stages.

Do not sacrifice the visual quality of the game just to add more features quickly.

FINAL GOAL

Create Rival Circuit, an original, detailed, colorful 2D pixel-art arcade fighting game with:

20 unique playable fighters.
7 beautifully illustrated arenas.
Fluid and responsive combat.
Intelligent CPU opponents.
Detailed character animations.
Unique special attacks.
Living environments.
A day-and-night cycle.
Original retro arcade music.
Unlockable outfits and cosmetics.
Arcade and Championship modes.
A reliable save system.
Fully functional mobile touchscreen controls.

The finished product should feel like a complete, carefully developed arcade fighting game with its own original identity, memorable characters, and high-quality visual presentation.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
